page: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This configuration is paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core and specialized computing capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier (top 10%), while the multi-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25%. Software compilation with Clang and ray tracing workloads on Geekbench also register strong performance in the top 25%, alongside the PassMark CPU physics test. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall within the average range (middle 50%), as do Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and LLM inference speeds for 135M and 7B models. However, single-threaded gzip compression is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25%.

This instance offers a balanced, high-density hardware profile suitable for memory-intensive and database workloads without the premium cost of specialized GPU hardware. The combination of 256 GB of RAM, 32 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs, and 1600 GB of fast NVMe SSD storage makes it well-suited for hosting relational databases, executing software compilation pipelines, running multi-threaded simulation workloads, and managing medium-scale web serving applications.
